sections.title: The Dimensional Paradox (0:00-0:45)
lecture_lines: A line has length, a plane has area.
Can one continuous line fill a 2D square?
Intuition says no, but math says yes.
We bridge dimensions with space-filling curves.
[Asset: Initial_Setup_Animation]

sections.title: The Peano Curve Construction (0:45-2:00)
lecture_lines: Start with a simple grid of squares.
Trace a path through each subdivision.
Recursion creates infinite complexity.
[Asset: Peano_Recursive_Trace]

sections.title: The Hilbert Curve: Efficiency in Recursion (2:00-3:15)
lecture_lines: Hilbert curves are a more efficient alternative.
The L-shape logic preserves spatial locality.
Points close on line remain close in space.
[Asset: Hilbert_L_Shape_Evolution]

sections.title: Real-World Applications (3:15-4:30)
lecture_lines: Curves optimize database indexing and storage.
They also enhance image processing tasks.
Locality helps computers access data faster.
[Asset: Application_Pixel_Sorting]

sections.title: Conclusion and Intuitive Summary (4:30-5:00)
lecture_lines: Space-filling curves flatten higher dimensions.
Nature uses these to maximize surface area.
Fractals pack complexity into minimal volumes.
[Asset: Conclusion_Nature_Overlay]
